types.embedding_query_text: ArtMovement: A collective of artists working together to establish a distinct stylistic or thematic approach to art. Also called ArtisticCollective, CreativeGroup, VisualArtGroup. Examples: Group of Seven, Indian Group of Seven, The Group of Seven, Professional Native Indian Artists Incorporated.

chosen_type.label: ArtMovement
chosen_type.definition: A collective of artists working together to establish a distinct stylistic or thematic approach to art.
chosen_type.justification: Minted as no schema.org class directly represents an art movement as a collective of artists. PerformingGroup (an Organization of performers) is the closest parent for a group of artists.

candidates.label: VisualArtwork
candidates.comment: A creative work that is primarily visual in nature, such as a painting, sculpture, or photograph. Also called art piece, visual art, artwork. Examples: Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa, a Rodin sculpture, an Ansel Adams photograph.

candidates.label: MediaReviewItem
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an item or group of items treated as a single unit for evaluation within a MediaReview. Also called reviewed media unit, content item for review, media subject. Examples: a specific viral video, a collection of related images, a particular news clip.

candidates.label: VisualArtsEvent
candidates.comment: An event related to visual arts, such as an exhibition, gallery opening, or art fair. Also called art exhibition, gallery event, visual art show. Examples: a painting exhibition, a sculpture display, a photography festival.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being, typically with a name and role in a specific context. Also called Individual, Artist, Curator. Examples: FH Varley, Katerina Atanassova, Tom Thomson, Jackson Beardy.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Person class matches the definition of an individual human being with examples aligning to the mentions.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: Researcher
candidates.comment: A Researcher is an Audience type representing individuals engaged in scientific or academic inquiry. Also called scientist, academic, scholar. Examples: a university professor, a lab scientist, a PhD student, an independent scholar.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

types.embedding_query_text: Painting: A two-dimensional artwork created through the application of paint on a surface. Also called Artwork, CanvasWork, VisualRepresentation. Examples: Stormy Weather, Georgian Bay.

chosen_type.label: Painting
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Painting class directly matches the definition of a two-dimensional artwork created with paint.

candidates.label: Painting
candidates.comment: A Painting, as a CreativeWork, is an artwork created by applying paint to a surface. Also called artwork, canvas, oil painting. Examples: Leonardo da Vinci's 'Mona Lisa', a watercolor landscape, an abstract acrylic painting. Distinct from Photograph, which is an image captured by a camera.

candidates.label: PaintAction
candidates.comment: A PaintAction, as a CreateAction, is the act of producing a painting, typically using paint and canvas. Also called painting, art creation, artistic rendering. Examples: painting a portrait, creating a landscape artwork, applying paint to a wall. Distinct from DrawAction, which typically involves lines and pencils.

candidates.label: VisualArtwork
candidates.comment: A creative work that is primarily visual in nature, such as a painting, sculpture, or photograph. Also called art piece, visual art, artwork. Examples: Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa, a Rodin sculpture, an Ansel Adams photograph.

candidates.label: CoverArt
candidates.comment: CoverArt is the visual artwork displayed on the outer surface of a CreativeWork, such as a book, album, or magazine. Also called album cover, book jacket, magazine cover, artwork. Examples: The cover of "Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band," the dust jacket of "To Kill a Mockingbird," the poster for a movie.

candidates.label: VisualArtsEvent
candidates.comment: An event related to visual arts, such as an exhibition, gallery opening, or art fair. Also called art exhibition, gallery event, visual art show. Examples: a painting exhibition, a sculpture display, a photography festival.

chosen_type.label: TimePeriod
chosen_type.definition: A span of time defined by a specific calendar year or decade.
chosen_type.justification: Minted as schema.org's Duration represents time spans but not named calendar periods like '1920s' or '1921'.

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

types.embedding_query_text: Museum: An institution dedicated to the collection, preservation, and exhibition of cultural artifacts and artworks. Also called Gallery, ArtInstitution, CulturalCenter. Examples: The National Gallery of Canada.

chosen_type.label: Museum
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Museum class aligns with the definition of a cultural institution for preserving and exhibiting artifacts.

candidates.label: Museum
candidates.comment: A Museum is a civic structure dedicated to preserving and exhibiting artifacts, art, or scientific specimens. Also called gallery, exhibition hall, cultural institution. Examples: The Louvre, Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, local art gallery. Distinct from Library, which primarily lends books and media.

candidates.label: ArtGallery
candidates.comment: An ArtGallery is an EntertainmentBusiness that displays and often sells works of art. Also called gallery, art exhibition space, fine art dealer. Examples: The Louvre, a local contemporary art gallery, a commercial art dealership, a pop-up exhibition space.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

candidates.label: ExhibitionEvent
candidates.comment: An ExhibitionEvent is an Event type focused on displaying items, such as at a museum, library, or tradeshow. Also called exhibit, show, display event. Examples: An art exhibition at a gallery, a historical display at a museum, a trade show for new technologies, a book fair.

candidates.label: Aquarium
candidates.comment: An Aquarium is a CivicStructure, typically a public facility, where aquatic animals and plants are kept and displayed. Also called public aquarium, marine life center, oceanarium. Examples: Monterey Bay Aquarium, Georgia Aquarium, a local fish exhibit.

types.embedding_query_text: Event: A planned or significant occurrence with a specific time and context. Also called Occasion, Gathering, Exhibition. Examples: The British Empire Exhibition, Wembley Exhibition.

chosen_type.label: Event
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's general Event class matches the broad definition of a planned or significant occurrence.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

types.embedding_query_text: Date Examples: 2026-07-07, Group of Seven Day.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's Date datatype directly represents the calendar date format in the mention '2026-07-07'.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: EventAttendanceModeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EventAttendanceModeEnumeration is an Enumeration of modes for organizing an event, indicating whether it is online or offline. Also called attendance type, event format, participation mode. Examples: OnlineEventAttendanceMode, OfflineEventAttendanceMode, MixedEventAttendanceMode.

chosen_type.label: Ethnicity
chosen_type.definition: A classification representing a cultural or ancestral group identity.
chosen_type.justification: Minted as schema.org lacks a class for ethnicity; Enumeration is the closest parent for categorical identities like 'Ojibway'.

candidates.label: CarUsageType
candidates.comment: An enumeration indicating a specific purpose or usage of a car. Also called vehicle use category, automobile purpose, car application type. Examples: Commercial rental, driving school, taxi service, personal use.

candidates.label: UKNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United Kingdom. Also called UK charity type, British non-profit category, UK voluntary sector classification. Examples: a registered charity, a community interest company (CIC), a benevolent society.

candidates.label: BoardingPolicyType
candidates.comment: An Enumeration representing different policies used by airlines for boarding passengers. Also called airline boarding rule, boarding group type, flight boarding policy. Examples: "Zone boarding", "Group boarding", "Priority boarding", "Family boarding".

candidates.label: GenderType
candidates.comment: A GenderType is an Enumeration of genders. Also called sex, gender identity. Examples: Male, Female, NonBinary.

candidates.label: MapCategoryType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of different categories or kinds of maps. Also called map type, map classification, cartography category. Examples: "RoadMap", "SatelliteMap", "TerrainMap", "HybridMap".

types.embedding_query_text: IndigenousTribe Examples: Chippewas of Nawash Unceded First Nation.

chosen_type.label: IndigenousTribe
chosen_type.definition: An Indigenous tribe or First Nation community recognized as a distinct ethnic and cultural group.
chosen_type.justification: Minted as schema.org's Organization class is the most relevant parent for structured Indigenous communities like 'Chippewas of Nawash Unceded First Nation'.

mentions: Chippewas of Nawash Unceded First Nation

candidates.label: NLNonprofitType
candidates.comment: NLNonprofitType is an enumeration for specific non-profit organization types originating from the Netherlands. Also called Dutch non-profit type, Netherlands charity classification. Examples: ANBI (Algemeen Nut Beogende Instelling), SBBI (Sociaal Belang Behartigende Instelling). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a general enumeration for non-profit types.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: SingleFamilyResidence
candidates.comment: A type of house designed to be occupied by one family, typically detached from other homes. Also called detached house, single-family home, private residence. Examples: a suburban house with a yard, a standalone cottage, a bungalow.

candidates.label: FoodEstablishmentReservation
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishmentReservation is a Reservation to dine at a food-related business. Also called restaurant booking, table reservation, dining reservation. Examples: A confirmed table booking at a restaurant, a reservation for a cafe, a booking for a private dining event. Distinct from Offer, which describes the availability of tables for booking.

candidates.label: DENonprofitType
candidates.comment: DENonprofitType is an enumeration representing specific types of non-profit organizations recognized under German fiscal code, article 52. Also called German non-profit classification, AO 52 non-profit. Examples: A German charitable foundation, a registered German association for public benefit.

candidates.label: VirtualLocation
candidates.comment: An online or non-physical location where events can be attended, such as a webinar or online meeting. Also called online venue, remote location, digital space. Examples: a Zoom meeting room, a webinar platform, a virtual conference hall.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".
